writing.prompt:
Part I Writing (30 minutes)

Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay on the importance of critical thinking in education. You can cite examples to illustrate your point. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
writing.ideas: 审题思路:现象分析类(重要性 why 型)。结构:① 首段从信息过载的时代背景切入,指出知识易得但判断力稀缺;② 理由一:学术层面,批判性思维是区分「记住」与「理解」的标志,决定能否解决课本外的问题;③ 理由二:社会层面,它是公民素养的防线——鉴别虚假信息、不被情绪煽动;④ 结尾落到教育方法:课堂应多问「为什么」而非只给「是什么」,鼓励质疑标准答案。
writing.model:
In an age when any fact is one search away, education can no longer be measured by how much students memorise. The scarce resource is judgement, and that is precisely what critical thinking supplies.
Academically, the difference shows up the moment students leave the textbook. A graduate who has only practised finding the one correct answer freezes when the real world presents five plausible ones. Critical thinking—the habit of questioning assumptions, weighing evidence and tolerating uncertainty—is what turns knowledge into usable wisdom. Socially, its value is even sharper. Every day, headlines are engineered to provoke outrage before reflection. Students trained to ask "who benefits from my reaction?" and "what evidence would change my mind?" become citizens who are difficult to manipulate. That is not an academic luxury; it is a civic defence.
Schools can cultivate this deliberately: asking "why" more often than "what," rewarding good questions as much as good answers, and letting students defend positions they personally disagree with. Facts will keep changing throughout a lifetime; the ability to examine them will not.
writing.notes: 亮点:① 首句 any fact is one search away 精准概括时代特征;② turns knowledge into usable wisdom 名言式表达;③ 设问式论证 who benefits from my reaction / what evidence would change my mind 具体可感;④ 结尾 facts will keep changing... the ability to examine them will not 对仗收束。加分表达:the scarce resource is judgement, engineered to provoke outrage, a civic defence。

listening.intro:
Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

【听力原文】
M: Sara, you have taken four online courses. Worth it?
W: Two were excellent, two were a waste of money. The difference was not the platform—it was whether the instructor designed for online.
M: What does that mean exactly?
W: Bad ones just filmed lectures and posted them. Good ones broke everything into ten-minute segments with quizzes in between, so you cannot drift away.
M: My problem is staying motivated. There is no deadline pressure in a video.
W: Then pick courses with live sessions or study groups. Human accountability beats willpower every time.
M: Good tip. I will also write a one-page summary after each module.
W: That is the technique top students use. Output beats input.
listening.questions:
1. How many of the woman's online courses were worthwhile?
A) None.
B) Two.
C) Three.
D) All four.

2. What distinguished the good courses?
A) Famous instructors.
B) Lower prices.
C) Design with short segments and quizzes.
D) Longer videos.

3. What is the man's main problem?
A) Staying motivated.
B) Paying for courses.
C) Finding good platforms.
D) Writing summaries.

4. What does the woman say beats willpower?
A) One-page summaries.
B) Human accountability.
C) Deadline pressure.
D) Free courses.
listening.analysis:
1. B。女士说两门极好、两门浪费钱, worthwhile 的是两门。
2. C。好课程把内容切分成十分钟片段并穿插测验(broke everything into ten-minute segments with quizzes in between)。
3. A。男士的困难是 staying motivated,视频缺乏截止日期的压力。
4. B。女士说 Human accountability beats willpower every time(人际督促胜过意志力)。

listening.intro:
Questions 5 to 7 are based on the passage you have just heard.

【听力原文】
Group projects have a bad reputation among students, and educational research suggests the reputation is partly deserved—but not for the reason most people assume. The problem is rarely teamwork itself; it is uneven participation. In study after study, the same pattern appears: one or two students carry the project while others contribute the minimum.
Psychologists call this social loafing, and it grows when individual contributions cannot be seen. When the final grade is shared, the rational strategy for a busy student is to do less, and even conscientious students slow down when they see others relaxing.
The fix is structural, not moral. Instructors who assign clear individual roles, require peer evaluations, and grade components separately report far higher satisfaction and better outcomes. The lesson extends beyond the classroom: any team that wants genuine cooperation must make each member's contribution visible and accountable.
listening.questions:
5. What is the real problem with group projects?
A) Teamwork is outdated.
B) Uneven participation.
C) Projects are too hard.
D) Students dislike each other.

6. What is "social loafing"?
A) Studying in the library.
B) Contributing less when effort cannot be seen.
C) Helping teammates constantly.
D) Grading others unfairly.

7. What fix do effective instructors use?
A) Moral lectures.
B) Bigger groups.
C) Clear roles and separate grading.
D) Easier projects.
listening.analysis:
5. B。研究指出问题很少是团队合作本身,而是参与不均(uneven participation)。
6. B。社会惰化指当个人贡献无法被看见时,个体倾向于减少投入。
7. C。有效的教师分配清晰个人角色、要求同伴互评、分开给分(clear individual roles, peer evaluations, grade components separately)。

listening.intro:
Questions 8 to 10 are based on the lecture you have just heard.

【听力原文】
Today's lecture concerns digital skills and employment. A common assumption is that digital skills matter only in tech jobs. Labour-market data tells a different story.
Analysts who examined millions of job postings found that roles requiring basic digital competence—spreadsheets, data interpretation, online collaboration—advertised salaries roughly twenty percent higher than comparable roles without that requirement, even in traditional sectors like retail and administration. In other words, digital literacy has become a wage premium across the whole economy, not just inside Silicon Valley.
The second finding is about direction of change. Postings mentioning AI-related tools tripled between 2021 and 2024, and the growth is fastest in marketing, finance and human resources. The implication for students is not that everyone must become a programmer; it is that everyone must become a competent user of intelligent tools. The most valuable employees of the next decade will be those who can describe a problem precisely enough for a machine to help solve it. That skill—clear problem description—is learned in the humanities as much as in engineering, which is why interdisciplinary graduates are quietly becoming the hardest to replace.
listening.questions:
8. What did the analysts find about salaries?
A) Tech jobs pay twenty percent more.
B) Roles requiring digital skills pay more across all sectors.
C) Retail pays less than administration.
D) Digital skills do not affect pay.

9. What happened to AI-related job postings between 2021 and 2024?
A) They halved.
B) They stayed flat.
C) They tripled.
D) They disappeared.

10. What skill will make employees hard to replace?
A) Writing code from scratch.
B) Describing problems precisely for machines to help.
C) Memorising data.
D) Avoiding AI tools.
listening.analysis:
8. B。研究发现要求基础数字技能的岗位薪水高出约百分之二十,且遍及零售、行政等传统行业。
9. C。提及 AI 工具的岗位招聘在 2021 到 2024 年间增长了两倍(tripled)。
10. B。讲座结论:最难得的人才的是能精确描述问题、让机器协助解决的人(describe a problem precisely enough for a machine to help solve)。

reading.title: Does Collaboration Really Make Us Smarter?
reading.passage:
Brainstorming sessions have been a fixture of office life since the 1940s, when an advertising executive claimed that groups generate more ideas than individuals working alone. Decades of research, however, have repeatedly found the opposite: people brainstorming in groups produce fewer ideas, and fewer good ones, than the same number of people thinking separately whose ideas are later pooled.
Psychologists identify three culprits. Production blocking occurs when only one person can speak at a time; ideas that surface mid-sentence evaporate while their owner waits for a turn. Evaluation apprehension makes people self-censor, quietly discarding unusual suggestions for fear of looking foolish. And social matching nudges the group toward the average: once the first few ideas establish a theme, later contributions unconsciously imitate them.
None of this means teamwork is useless; it means teamwork is mistimed. The most effective teams alternate between solitary generation and collective selection. Software companies have quietly adopted this pattern: engineers write design documents alone, then attack them together. Classrooms, too, report better results when students think silently for two minutes before discussion begins.
The broader lesson applies to any creative work: the group is an excellent editor and a poor first draft. Protect the solitude that generates ideas, and save the room for the moment when ideas need to be tested.
reading.questions:
1. What did the advertising executive claim in the 1940s?
A) Groups produce more ideas than individuals.
B) Individuals are more creative than groups.
C) Brainstorming wastes office time.
D) Ideas should be written silently.

2. What is production blocking?
A) Fear of looking foolish.
B) Ideas evaporating while waiting for a turn.
C) Copying the first idea.
D) Refusing to speak.

3. What does social matching nudge groups toward?
A) The most unusual idea.
B) The average theme.
C) Complete disagreement.
D) Silent work.

4. What pattern do effective teams use?
A) Constant group discussion.
B) Alternating solitary generation and collective selection.
C) No evaluation of ideas.
D) One person deciding.

5. What is the passage's broader lesson?
A) Groups are excellent first drafts.
B) Protect solitude for generating ideas.
C) Brainstorming should be banned.
D) Creativity cannot be taught.
reading.analysis:
1. A。第一段:1940 年代广告主管声称群体比单独个体产生更多想法。
2. B。产生阻塞指一次只能一人发言,等待轮次期间灵感蒸发。
3. B。社会模仿使群体趋向平均:前几个想法定下主题后,后续贡献不自觉地模仿。
4. B。第三段:高效团队在独自产生与集体筛选之间交替(solitary generation and collective selection)。
5. B。结尾:群体是出色的编辑却是糟糕的初稿——要保护产生想法的独处时光。

translation.prompt:
请将以下中文段落翻译成英文:

中国劳动年龄人口的平均受教育年限已超过十年,高等教育普及程度达到发达国家平均水平。职业教育与普通教育同等重要的观念逐渐深入人心,越来越多的年轻人愿意选择职业技术学院。政府近年来大力建设高水平职业院校,推动产教融合、校企合作,旨在培养更多高素质技术技能人才,以满足制造业升级对劳动力的新需求。
translation.reference: The average years of schooling among China's working-age population now exceed ten, and the popularisation of higher education has reached the average level of developed countries. The idea that vocational education is as important as general education is gradually taking root, and a growing number of young people are willing to choose vocational colleges. In recent years, the government has made great efforts to build high-level vocational institutions and promote the integration of industry and education as well as cooperation between schools and enterprises, aiming to cultivate more highly skilled personnel to meet the new demand for labour created by manufacturing upgrading.
translation.notes: 要点:①「受教育年限」译为 average years of schooling,是教育统计标准术语;②「深入人心」意译为 taking root(生根),比 entering hearts 准确得多;③「产教融合」即 the integration of industry and education;④「校企合作」即 cooperation between schools and enterprises;⑤「高素质技术技能人才」译为 highly skilled personnel,避免逐字堆叠 talented skillful people。
